messages:
pagerduty-bot: 🔔 P1 triggered: inferpool-usw experiencing NotReady surge — ~20% nodes NotReady, impact on hosted inference. Paging #eng-oncall. https://pd.example/incidents/PD-4567
maya: I’m oncall, picking this up. any immediate customer-facing symptoms?
sam: support: seeing increased 5xx rates and tail latency for US hosted API since 11:07 UTC. ~3 customers reporting degraded throughput.
ryan: checking nodes now — kubelet restarts on several GPU nodes. dmesg on node infer-usw-4 shows repeated NVRM errors and a kernel OOM before kubelet restart. logs: ```Apr 12 11:06:52 kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, GPU at 0xdeadbeef
Apr 12 11:07:01 kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 24105 (serving-runtime) total-vm:...
Apr 12 11:07:03 systemd: kubelet.service: main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL```
alice: I'm cordoning nodes with kubelet churn to stop new pods landing. cordon: infer-usw-3, infer-usw-4. draining with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data.
ops-runner: Executed: `kubectl cordon infer-usw-3 && kubectl drain infer-usw-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m` — drain succeeded for pod evictions, some longs: batcher pods requeued.
ryan: rerouting: updating traffic policy to steer US traffic to eu-west and dedicated capacity. ETA for traffic cutover ~2m. Also reducing concurrent request batcher size to avoid OOM pressure.
sam: Notifying affected customers: sent initial advisory to Customer A and B (IDs redacted). They'll see degraded latency while we failover.
maya: quick diag, which kernel/driver combo are these nodes on?
ryan: nodes are on ubuntu-22.04 + nvidia-driver 535.42.07, K8s 1.27. kubelet logs show repeated crashloop after OOM, then kubelet-watchdog triggers restart. suspect a workload pattern suddenly allocating large KV cache entries.
alice: scaling dedicated pool by +3 G4 instances via infra autoscale override to buy headroom. Applied: `infractl capacity adjust --pool dedicated-usw --delta +3 --reason "NotReady surge"`
infra-bot: autoscale: dedicated-usw +3 requested, provisioning started (instances: 3 requested, 0 active).
ryan: mitigation checklist: 1) cordon/drain unstable nodes (done for 2), 2) steer traffic to eu/dedicated (in progress), 3) reduce batch size + disable aggressive caching for hosted model variants (in progress), 4) investigate kernel OOM cause + collect heap dumps.
ops-runner: running `kubectl logs -n infra serving-runtime-xyz -c runtime` on a restarted node returned: ```panic: runtime: out of memory\ngoroutine 1 [running]:\nmain.start()...``` capturing logs to s3: s3://redwood-ops/incidents/PD-4567/logs/7193/
sam: customer impact update: after initial steer, 5xxs dropped ~80% for affected customers; some still see higher p99 latency ~2.1s vs baseline 0.9s.
maya: keeping nodes cordoned until we validate driver/kernel patch; can we repro with a small load?
ryan: spinning up a canary in a sandbox with same image + KMS model to reproduce; also raising eviction threshold on the problematic nodes to avoid premature OOM if kernel misreports memory. doing: `kubectl patch node infer-usw-4 -p '{"spec":{"evictionHard":{"memory.available":"100Mi"}}}'`
alice: kernel engineers pulled dmesg + kdump; one node shows repeated GPU resets, driver stacktrace indicates potential firmware regression. opening bug with hw vendor.
ops-runner: infra autoscale reported 2/3 new dedicated instances active, routing now ~65% of non-critical traffic to them.
ryan: temporary fallback enabled: hosted API now prefers quantized model variant with smaller KV footprint for US tier. config pushed via feature flag.
sam: will continue customer comms with a follow-up in 30m.
maya: any need to page kernel/firmware oncall?
alice: yes, paging hw-oncall, providing collected logs + kdump.
infra-bot: hw-oncall paging: ticket HW-2024 created and assigned.
ryan: next steps: 1) keep nodes cordoned, 2) monitor p95/p99 and 5xxs for 30m, 3) if stable, gradually uncordon one node at a time after driver rollback or workaround, 4) postmortem owner: ryan.
maya: acknowledged. handing off to daytime oncall in 25m. adding runbook link: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kubelet-heartbeat-flip
sam: impact summary to stakeholders scheduled in 45m.
ops-runner: last check: 5xxs back to baseline for most customers, dedicated capacity handling ~40% of traffic. Keeping thread open for rollback validation.
maya: closing pager for now — will reopen if NotReady count increases. :thumbsup:
